reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in replacing manual landmark annotation with automated edge-based registration. The method begins by generating a synthetic dictionary of edge maps and corresponding homographies through simulated camera motions. This dictionary is built from a reference image and warped versions to emulate diverse viewpoints. For each new broadcast frame, the system computes its edge map and performs a nearest neighbor search against the dictionary to find the best-matching homography. Temporal stabilization refines this estimate by enforcing smoothness across video frames. The registration process is formulated as a minimization problem where the objective balances fidelity to the synthetic edge map and regularization of camera motion. This approach avoids reliance on sparse point correspondences, which are often absent in broadcast video. The method's robustness stems from leveraging structured field lines rather than arbitrary visual features. Failure modes include occlusion of line markings, extreme camera motion beyond the synthetic range, and poor illumination affecting edge detection quality.
